title: Sequence-of-returns risk: the order matters
objectives: Explain sequence-of-returns risk with the two-retiree illustration.
Say why retirees need a cash and debt buffer.
body_md:
The order of returns matters once money is coming out. Two retirees, each with ₹1 Cr, withdraw ₹5 L in year one, rising 6% a year. Both get exactly the same returns over 20 years, just in a different order (illustrative).

| Retiree | Returns | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Two falls of 15% in years 1–2, then 12% a year | Money runs out in about year 19 |
| B | 12% a year, then two falls of 15% in years 19–20 | About ₹2.06 Cr still left after 20 years |

A fall early in retirement does lasting damage, because units are sold at low prices to pay expenses. That is why retirees need a cash and debt buffer.
example: Retiree A: two falls of 15% in years 1–2, then 12% a year → money runs out in about year 19. Retiree B: 12% a year, then two falls in years 19–20 → about ₹2.06 Cr still left after 20 years. Same returns, different order.
say: Early losses in withdrawals do more damage.
Units sold low to pay bills cause lasting damage.
never: A fall late in retirement is worse than an early fall.

o: Early losses in withdrawals do more damage
check.why: Early losses in withdrawals do more damage. Units are sold low to pay bills.
